partner_context.their_ambition: Grab is Southeast Asia's everyday super-app — mobility, deliveries, and payments in one. Mobility is the original engine and still the highest-margin business (~$1.22B, ~36% of 2025 revenue), and the 2026 playbook is 'Growth with Purpose': defend the category, premiumise, and keep widening the multimodal map across all eight countries Grab serves.
partner_context.their_pressure: Ride-hail on land is maturing and increasingly contested. The next leg of high-margin growth comes from new surfaces and premium tiers — not from squeezing the road. Meanwhile every coastal megacity Grab owns is hemmed in by water that no super-app has ever monetised.
partner_context.where_navier_fits: Water is the only transport surface in Southeast Asia no one owns yet. Navier turns it into a Grab tier: a software-defined foiling fleet, booked in-app, premium-priced, on the densest coastal and cross-border corridors in the region — the same network model already ramping in the Maldives.

hero.title: Grab × Navier — the black-car network, on the water
hero.subtitle: Southeast Asia's super-app already owns the demand. Water is the only transport surface no one owns yet.
hero.what_we_do_together: We launch a Grab-branded foiling water tier across Southeast Asia's densest coastal and cross-border corridors — booked in-app, premium-priced, region-wide and category-defining. Navier brings the software-defined hydrofoiling fleet and the network playbook now proven in the Maldives; Grab brings the demand, the app, the wallet, and the regional reach. Together we turn slow, weather-exposed ferry crossings into fast, smooth, on-demand water trips — and claim the category before anyone else does.

why_now: Foiling lifts the hull clear of the water: faster, dramatically more efficient per passenger-mile, smooth and near-silent, hybrid-capable with no charging-infrastructure dependency, and autonomy-ready. A ~100-vessel network is already ramping in the Maldives (WSJ/Bloomberg, 2026), and Singapore's regulator is mandating clean harbour craft from 2030. The category gets claimed cluster-by-cluster — and Southeast Asia's cross-border seas are the next surface.
multimodal_fit: Grab already runs the hardest parts: real-time demand, dispatch, dynamic pricing, a trusted wallet, and a driver-partner network. A foiling water tier slots straight in — same app, same wallet, captain-partners instead of driver-partners, the water leg booked door-to-door with the GrabCar to and from the pier. Navier is simply the missing surface in a multimodal map Grab already operates.

differentiation.vs_status_quo: Today's crossings are scheduled, slow, diesel, and the first thing cancelled in bad weather. A foiling tier is on-demand, fast, near-silent, low/zero-emission, and — because the hull flies above the chop — runs smooth on the days ferries don't.
differentiation.why_navier: Software-defined and autonomy-ready — the same software-first instincts as Grab. A factory in Turkey for regional supply, and a ~100-vessel at-scale network already proving the model in the Maldives.

proof_points.claim: The network model is real and at scale.
proof_points.evidence: ~100 vessels / $100M / 3-year phasing with JIH Global in the Maldives — 'a black-car network on the water'.

proof_points.claim: Regulators are pulling marine toward clean fleets.
proof_points.evidence: From 2030 all new harbour craft in the Port of Singapore must be fully electric / B100 / net-zero-fuel capable; net-zero harbour craft by 2050.
Millions cross Singapore↔Riau each year; Bintan alone draws 350k+ tourists annually — today on slow ferries.
~$1.22B, ~36% of 2025 revenue; first full-year net profit in 2025 — a premium water tier compounds the best segment.

objections.response: Every Singapore cross-border crossing (Batam ~12 nm, Bintan ~30 nm, Desaru ~28 nm) sits well inside the Pioneer II 70 nm all-electric envelope. The longer regional legs (Bali–Lombok–Komodo, Phuket–Langkawi) run on the Quanta-LR hybrid — 2,000 nm at 20 kts, no charging infrastructure required.

objections.concern: What about sea state and weather?
objections.response: Foils lift the hull clear of the surface, so the ride is smooth where displacement ferries pound and cancel. The platform is more weather-tolerant, not less — that reliability is the premium.

Software-defined controls, a clear first-of-class certification path, and an operating record across the US and now the Maldives. Singapore's clean-harbour-craft push makes it the strongest certification beachhead in SEA.
Sheltered-strait routing plus Quanta-LR range give the network the flexibility to keep running and reposition through monsoon windows.

phases.rationale: Start in the world's busiest port, where the regulator is already mandating clean harbour craft — the cleanest first-of-class story in SEA, and a dense home market to prove utilisation before crossing a border.
phases.narrative: Five Pioneer II vessels on Singapore's highest-demand inner-water corridors, booked in the Grab app. Small fleet, dense utilisation, a clean first-of-class certification story in the regulator's own backyard.

phases.label: Phase 2 — The cross-border crossings
featured_routes: Singapore ↔ Desaru Coast (Johor) — the under-served Malaysia crossing
phases.rationale: This is the corridor no one owns. Singapore↔Bintan carries 350k+ resort tourists a year on slow ferries; Singapore↔Desaru is barely served by sea yet drowns in Causeway traffic by road. Cross-border, in-app, premium water is the defensible category — and it goes to both Indonesia and Malaysia from day one.
phases.narrative: We light up the crossings: Bintan's Lagoi resort coast and the under-served Desaru/Johor corridor, plus high-frequency Batam. Same app, same wallet, door-to-door with GrabCar either side — the cross-border water layer of the super-app, reaching Indonesia and Malaysia at once.

phases.rationale: From three proven clusters, the same playbook extends to every coastal market Grab serves — starting with the Philippines, where the government is itself reviving urban ferries (Pasig/MAPALLA) and the archipelago is tailor-made for a foiling network.
phases.narrative: Manila's bay and river, then Cebu–Bohol–Palawan — the archipelago that ferries serve worst and foiling serves best. The water layer of the super-app, region-wide.

the_ask.navier_brings: The software-defined foiling fleet (Pioneer II + Quanta-LR), the network and operations playbook proven in the Maldives, captain training, and the first-of-class certification path.
the_ask.partner_brings: Demand and dispatch through the Grab app, the wallet, the brand, and the regulatory relationships across each market.
the_ask.next_step: A Singapore pilot MOU: co-define the in-app water tier on three corridors, then scale to the cross-border crossings.

close.title: One app. One region-wide water network. The whole region next.
close.body: Singapore proves it, the Bintan and Desaru crossings make it cross-border, and Bali + Phuket make it regional. From there the same playbook extends across every coastal market Grab already serves — the water layer of Southeast Asia's super-app.

why_navier_now.step_change: Hydrofoiling lifts the hull clear of the water, so a Navier vessel flies instead of plowing through chop - roughly 10x more efficient than a conventional planing boat, faster (30+ kt cruise), and dramatically smoother and quieter. It's software-defined and autonomy-ready, so the same fleet keeps getting better and cheaper to run over time. A step-change in marine mobility, not an incremental faster boat.
why_navier_now.no_new_infrastructure: Navier rides on infrastructure that already exists - the open ocean and the berths and jetties already in use. No vertiports, no new rights-of-way, no tunnels or tracks. Pioneer II needs only a berth pedestal; the Quanta-LR hybrid needs no charging infrastructure at all. That's the fundamental contrast with flying taxis and other new-infrastructure modes: nothing to permit, build, or wait for.
why_navier_now.the_moment: Three forces just converged: the technology crossed from prototype to platform (10 vessels delivered, 4,000+ flight hours, 2025 production sold out), decarbonization mandates turned legacy diesel fleets into stranded liabilities, and the hybrid removed the 'no charging at the islands' excuse. Autonomy is arriving on the water before the road. The marine layer is being claimed cluster-by-cluster right now.
